source.title: What's the plan? Metrics for implicit planning in LLMs and their application to rhyme generation and question answering
source.authors: Jim Maar; D. Paperno; Callum McDougall; Neel Nanda

record.tranche_reason: Tests implicit planning with localized activation steering and causal interventions, using different methods and quantitative measures from the cited Claude 3.5 Haiku cross-layer-transcoder study.
record.gate_note: The paper reports rhyme-family steering, rhyme-word regeneration, question-answer steering, article choice, attention ablation, activation patching, and subject-verb agreement results. Results it cites from other studies are not recorded. Layer and position choices used to select steering locations are not recorded as outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study uses mean-activation-difference steering, patching and ablation, not cross-layer transcoders, to ask whether open-weight models (1B–32B) plan rhymes and answers ahead. Its own results bear on V4, V5 (noun QA, subject-verb arithmetic QA) and V6 (plan vs improvisation, intermediate-token effects). None of its authors' papers is an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but incomplete. The authors claim implicit planning is a general mechanism, present from 1B parameters, though weaker in smaller models. Planning metrics rise with size and instruction tuning. Mean-difference steering at the line end or question manipulates the rhyme or answer and the intermediate tokens. In Gemma2 9B a two-head attention circuit carries the rhyme plan, and question answering uses a distinct circuit.
record.recipe_differences: The paper replaces the cited study’s cross-layer-transcoder analysis with mean activation difference steering and quantitative regeneration and behavior metrics; it also includes activation patching, attention ablation, probing, and SAE examples.
record.method_sensitivity: Rhyme steering on the newline is effective only for selected models, while last-word steering works across models; newline steering is somewhat less effective. In question answering, steering effects differ between suggestive and neutral questions, and instruction-tuned models show stronger effects on neutral questions. Specific-word steering is weaker than rhyme-family steering. Steering effects vary with model size and tuning stage.
record.problems: Many main comparisons are presented as plots without numerical values in the text; the paper reports no uncertainty estimates in the included results. Noun-answer steering on suggestive questions only partly recovers baseline frequencies. The subject-verb agreement experiment is small, with 80 questions and 10 test examples, and is reported for Gemma3 27B only. Specific-word steering is limited in the two tested models.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted for the 60-row limit. Figures with per-model values are represented only where the text gives an aggregate or explicitly identifies models with different outcomes; unreported figure values were not transcribed individually.

untested.parts: No frontier or closed model is tested. Claude Haiku results are only cited.
No decoding of future tokens from a single hidden state.
Does not separate features computed for later positions from by-product features.
Chess, Sokoban and non-transformer architectures are not tested.
Open attribution graphs are not used.

missing.what: Probability-based metrics showing how early in the second line the steered and unsteered distributions diverge: top-1 difference, high-KL fraction, tokens after first divergence. These bear on how far ahead the plan acts.
Tokenization control: single-token first-line subset and embedding-similarity check, ruling out last-token or embedding explanations of rhyme steering.
Per-model newline steering effectiveness: effective only in Gemma2 9B and Gemma3 27B.
SAE latent 5862 fires on the first-line newline but not the second, in Gemma2 9B. The Llama 3.1 8B counterpart does not fire on the newline.
Probe-weight steering examples (-ick to -ore) in Gemma2 9B.

record.verdict_notes: Main fixes: QA rows R6–R8 moved from V4 to V5. Table 1 patched and steered values are swapped in R12–R15. Table 3 column labels in R16–R19 give the original answer, not the target. Most aggregate results are figure-only, with no uncertainty reported. The subject-verb test set is 10 examples on one model. Figures 22–23 captions conflict with the text on neutral-question recovery.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests open-weight models, not a frontier model.
It does not directly measure whether a single hidden state can be decoded to predict tokens several positions ahead.
It does not distinguish features computed to help later positions from features arising as a side effect of next-token prediction.
It tests open-weight models with mean-activation-difference steering, but does not test the mechanism using open attribution graphs; probe- and SAE-based steering are shown only in limited examples.
It tests rhyme, noun question answering, and a subject-verb agreement task. It does not test chess, Sokoban, or other architectures.

It tests evidence for planning versus improvisation in one small question-answering task and reports weak steering for specific rhyme words. It does not establish that all planning is limited to a few tokens or is merely a local heuristic.
